items.stemHtml: A 47-year-old man with nephrotic syndrome from membranous nephropathy (PLA2R antibody positive; serum albumin 1.9 g/dL) has sudden left flank pain and gross hematuria. Two days later he notices a new soft, painless swelling in the left side of his scrotum that feels like a bag of worms when he stands and becomes smaller when he lies down. The right side is normal. Which of the following best explains the scrotal finding?

options.label: A
options.html: The left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein

options.label: B
options.html: The left gonadal vein drains directly into the inferior vena cava

options.label: C
options.html: The left renal artery compresses the left gonadal vein

options.label: D
options.html: The left renal vein passes behind the abdominal aorta

options.label: E
options.html: The left testicular artery arises from the left renal artery

items.explanationHtml:
Membranous nephropathy with heavy proteinuria and low albumin is the classic setting for renal vein thrombosis, which presents with flank pain and hematuria. The left testicular (gonadal) vein drains into the left renal vein, so a clot in the left renal vein raises pressure in the pampiniform plexus and produces a new left varicocele. The right gonadal vein enters the inferior vena cava directly, so the right side is spared.

Takeaway: a new left varicocele with flank pain points to left renal vein obstruction, because the left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein.

whyNot.B: It is the right gonadal vein that drains directly into the inferior vena cava.
whyNot.C: Arterial compression of the gonadal vein is not a recognised mechanism; nutcracker compression involves the renal vein between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery.
whyNot.D: The left renal vein normally passes in front of the aorta; a retroaortic course is an uncommon variant and would not explain an acute change.
whyNot.E: The testicular arteries arise from the aorta, and arterial anatomy does not explain venous congestion.

items.objective: Link renal vein thrombosis in nephrotic syndrome to a new left varicocele through gonadal venous drainage.
